data_source: Small specialized clinic with heavy MSP outsourcing (constructed from public NCSC/HSE/ENISA benchmarks)

answers.evidence: No designated NIS2 compliance officer; responsibility informally held by Practice Manager; no appointment record.
No board-level cyber oversight; directors rely on the IT managed-service provider (MSP); no cyber item in board minutes.
No ring-fenced cyber budget; security spend bundled into the monthly MSP retainer (MSP-CON-2024).
No board or director cyber-governance training undertaken.
Generic acceptable-use and IT policy supplied by MSP template (MSP-POL-001); not tailored or formally adopted.
MSP template covers acceptable use and basic access; supply chain, cryptography, continuity and measurement areas absent.
MSP performs informal annual review; no documented ISO 27005-style risk assessment owned by the clinic.
Key systems known informally (PACS/RIS, billing); no formal critical-asset register or classification.
No independent control audit or effectiveness testing on record.
MSP applies fixes reactively after issues; no documented post-incident review owned by the clinic.
MSP applies OS/security patching under managed-service SLA (MSP-SLA-2024, monthly cycle); clinic does not verify independently.
MSP runs cloud backups; clinic has never witnessed or signed off a restore test.
Ad-hoc phishing awareness emails; no mandatory enrolment or completion tracking.
MSP holds a partial device list; no clinic-maintained, reconciled inventory.
Pre-employment checks for clinical staff via HR; references and qualification checks retained.
Leaver access removal raised by email to MSP; no SLA, occasional delays observed.
MFA enabled on Microsoft 365 email and VPN; not enforced on PACS/RIS admin or MSP remote-management tooling.
Some role separation between clinical and admin staff; shared and over-privileged accounts still common; no least-privilege review.
Primary systems hosted in MSP/cloud data centre with physical security; on-site comms cabinet lockable.
Cloud-hosted data encrypted by provider default; local imaging shares and some endpoints unencrypted.
HTTPS/TLS for hosted applications and portal; SFTP for external image exchange.
MSP master services agreement exists but lacks explicit security SLAs, breach-notification or right-to-audit clauses.
MSP and software vendors not formally risk-assessed; no due-diligence questionnaires retained.
Informal vendor selection considers data-handling at a basic level; no documented secure-acquisition gate.
No clinic-owned incident response plan; assumption that the MSP 'will handle it'.
No incident exercise or tabletop ever conducted.
No capability or process to submit a 24h NIS2 early warning; no awareness of CSIRT contact route.
MSP provides basic endpoint protection and log monitoring; no clinic visibility of alerts or coverage.
No business continuity plan with RTO/RPO; downtime procedures undocumented.
No disaster-recovery test performed or evidenced.
